benefits.doc: The benefits home (agent_team E71-S2, Jordi's E71-A4 approval 2026-11-07): the first section of data/brief.md, `## Benefits`. Every persona is handed it with the brief, reads it as a key element and writes from it; the rule for writing a benefit is the recipe below (agent_team EPIC-71 L-1).
benefits.post_rule: A new post shows ONE benefit from the Benefits table, names its number in Benefit, opens on that benefit (what the user gets) and shows its What it does with the real screen and may ask a question after it. The benefit must be `works today`; a `half built` or `not built` line is never promised as working, only called coming soon. A post already approved or scheduled is not rewritten to fit this rule.
benefits.idea_rule: An idea may come without a benefit; the Writer names the one it demonstrates when it takes the idea. One benefit fans out into many posts across ideas and platforms.
recipe: Draft first: five lines or fewer on one screen, before any research.
If the voice matters and there is no example, ask for one or write one and say so.
Walk the product in the order the user meets it, one thing per line, five lines or fewer.
Each line pairs What it does (plain words: it writes, it holds, it answers) with the Benefit it brings (what the user gets, in their terms).
Plain words a user would say; no slogans, abstract nouns or method names; only this product, never another one the team posts for.
Mark each line works today, half built or not built, with a real screen.

When Jordi hands over his own lines ("here is an example, WDYT?"), they are the floor and the voice sample, never the deliverable (agent_team EPIC-71 L-2): write for the end user, not for him; show his version beside ours line by line, naming each change in a few words; add what his lines miss and one bolder alternative, so he picks from more than one option; read the lines to a cold reader first; after he approves, ask for his verdict on the result (did we add anything over his words?), since an approve alone is not one. Returning his words unchanged is not a draft.
benefits.discovery: What people say they want (a comment, a reply, a desk note) is noted with its link as an Observations line `L-<n> | … | proposed for the brief (Benefits): "<the line to add or change>"` when two notes agree; Jordi adds it to the Benefits table or says not now. Nobody but Jordi edits the table.

product.doc: The product deck (agent_team E78-S1, Jordi 2026-11-08: "what's the deck of the product? … that deck is like the landing page"): one part per slide, in his order, saying what we sell, to whom, for how much and how it differs. Separate from each campaign's deck (its spine's Brief). Every persona reads it at each wake beside its campaign's deck and never promises more than it says. It links, never copies: the benefit lines stay in data/brief.md (Benefits), the facts follow the live landing pages in the same commit when they change.
product.campaign_doc: Each campaign's own product deck (agent_team E78-S1 round 2, Jordi 2026-11-08: "product at highest level of the repo, and then inside the campaign, be able to specifically go to town about whatever we're promoting - product, service, promo"): what that campaign pushes, one part per slide, beside its strategy deck. It narrows the project's deck and never contradicts it; a campaign with none works from the project's deck and its Brief and says so.

jordi_part.heading: What Jordi said
jordi_part.doc: The part that keeps both decks alive (agent_team EPIC-81, Jordi 2026-11-08: "if I'm saying things that are kind of worth considering that they are made explicit in these decks so that in future iterations they will pop up"): the last part of the project's deck and of each campaign's deck, the lines of his voice notes worth keeping about that product or campaign, newest first, quoted as transcribed (a word in [brackets] fixes the transcriber), never a paraphrase, never invented. The day after a note, the host's voice-note reader (agent_team: the Input reviewer's daily run) appends them, one commit per repo; another world's decks get a desk note instead. Every persona reads it first at each wake (the host carries it ahead of the deck's cut) and raises a change it asks for elsewhere in Observations, never edits other parts on it.

metrics.doc: The metrics catalog (agent_team E78-S1, Jordi 2026-11-08: "a catalog of metrics … It cannot be randomly decided. It has to be living in one place … a campaign needs to have a metric attached to it"). One list of numbers a campaign may target; the host (the agent_team console) computes them and writes data/metrics.md at its hourly check, only when a number changed: the catalog with today's values, each campaign's target and where it stands, and one row per role (the number it wakes to move and the files it reads). Nobody edits data/metrics.md by hand. Every persona reads it and data/product.md at each wake.

A row for another platform or outside its period is not the campaign's (Campaign empty). Bound to the repo's root spine, leave Campaign empty

no_late_post.doc: A late post never goes out. Before you post a `scheduled` post, compare its Slot with now: if the slot passed more than 60 min ago and Jordi has not released it since (no `Approved <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> UTC` or `Post now <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> UTC` note in its Feedback dated at or after the slot), do NOT post it: move it `scheduled → held` (nothing else in the row) in its own commit and say so in your summary. It was missed while its campaign was retired or paused, you were off, or the egress was offline; Jordi's card then says "Its slot (… UTC) has passed. It is not posted." and he presses Post now or picks a new time. A post with his newer Approved or Post now note goes out at once: that is his Post now
no_late_post.undo: Jordi's Post now or Pick a new time on its card

own_campaign_posts.doc: A Publisher sends only its own campaign's posts. Whose a row is: its Campaign cell (the campaign's epic code, rule campaign_tag); an empty cell is the repo level's (the repo's root spine). Bound to a campaign, you act only on rows carrying its code; bound to the repo's root spine, on rows with no Campaign, plus the rows of a live campaign of this repo that has no Publisher of its own. Never post, expire, hold or delete any other row, and never a retired campaign's posts (its milestone settled, hidden from the sidebar): nobody sends them; they wait as they are until Jordi restores the campaign or tags the row for a live one. A Campaign naming no campaign of the repo is nobody's: leave it and say so in your summary. The agent_team console's wake prompt lists your rows in its Publisher brief, and its wake gate wakes you only for them

revise_requested.doc: Jordi's `Revise requested <when>: …` note in a held post's Feedback asks for a NEW VERSION for his review: redraft it (Text and Title, and its diagram when the note asks, as a new asset row), keep it `held` (never schedule it: only his `Approved` note lets it out) and start the row's Checks with `Revised <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> UTC` (the time of your redraft) so his console shows it ready for review again

dm_messages.doc: DMs and chat requests are not posts: they live in data/messages-ledger.md, never as posts-ledger rows. One Chats row per conversation (platform, our account, who, kind, link, started); each of their messages a `received` row (the text when it is one short line, else `summary: …`, at most 200 characters); your answer a `draft` row with its full text and Answers = their message. NEVER send a draft: Jordi's Send moves it `draft → scheduled` (his `Approved` note). On each wake send every `scheduled` reply exactly as written, dry run first, then for real, within the caps (10 DMs a day, 20 min between Reddit writes, 3 an hour); record the send in Result, move it `scheduled → posted` and the chat to `waiting` in one commit; a `pulled` one is never sent. A chat you leave alone by rule is its own Chats row in `left` with its Reason in plain words and its Link (a request whose text the platform hides until accepted: `hidden`, never accept it yourself); never bundle several chats in one row. Jordi's `Revise requested <when>: …` on a draft: write a new version (Text), keep it `draft`, start Checks with `Revised <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> UTC`. His `Draft requested` (or `Accept requested`: accept the request first) on a chat: draft a reply for his Send

link_present.doc: a post goes live with its link in the same commit

sent.doc: a sent reply records its send in Result (time, tool, dry run) in the same commit

intake.doc: Desk chat intake: every line Jordi says to the desk is one of these kinds. The desk sorts it into one kind, writes it where the kind says through the console's write API (commits as Jordi, EPICSPINE_PERSONA=Jordi), and replies with where it landed.
intake.unsure: Cannot tell the kind, or it could be two: ask Jordi one line back naming the two likeliest kinds; never write a guess.
intake.reply: Every reply names where it landed: the file and section as a link ({link}, a repo path with its #anchor), the line it added or changed, who acts on it next and when, and undo (revert that commit).

spine.doc: a new child epic under the root spine (spine_new.py), Status draft, its dependencies named in it

brief.label: Brief change
brief.recognise: changes the standing campaign, not one week and not one post: the objective, targets, audience, voice, a style rule, a phrase never to say, topic weights, the formats mix, an example liked or disliked, a hold rule
brief.example: never mention prices beyond what the site says
brief.acts: every persona reads it from its next wake
brief.reply: Brief, {section}: "{line}" ({link}). Every persona reads it from its next wake. Undo: revert {commit}.

key_message.label: Key message
key_message.recognise: a point to push, soften or drop across posts, or a new one; says more / less / stop about a message rather than a week's focus
key_message.acts: the Writer weighs it from its next wake; carried-by on the Brief shows which posts carry it
key_message.reply: Key message #{id} weight → {weight}: "{line}" ({link}). Carried-by shows on the Brief. Undo: revert {commit}.

priority.label: Priority
priority.recognise: what to highlight this week or this month, or a do / don't for this week only; has a time span (this week, this month, until a date)
priority.example: push the EpicSpine angle more this month
priority.acts: the Writer and the Scout weigh it from their next wake
priority.reply: Priority {id} for {period}: "{line}" ({link}). The Writer and Scout read it from their next wake ({next_wake}). Undo: revert {commit}.

idea.label: Idea
idea.recognise: one post Jordi wants made: a topic, an angle, a link or a screenshot to post about; one post can carry it
idea.example: post idea: how git log saved me from a bad memory
idea.acts: the Writer picks it up on its next wake: new → picked up → draft / posted, or parked with why
idea.reply: Added to My ideas as {id} (from: Jordi): "{line}" ({link}). The Writer picks it up on its next wake ({next_wake}); you see picked up → draft there and in the digest. Undo: revert {commit}.

big_idea.label: Big idea → epic
big_idea.recognise: more than one post can carry: it needs a new tool, a new persona, a video or several posts
big_idea.example: do a post with a demo video of shared memory across Claude and Codex
big_idea.acts: the Delivery manager plans it; Home shows it as a blocked card until what it waits on exists
big_idea.reply: That needs more than one post, so it is an epic: {code} "{title}" ({link}), waiting on {waits_on}. Home shows it as "blocked: {waits_on}". Nothing for you to do now. Undo: revert {commit}.

feedback.label: Feedback on a post
feedback.recognise: a verdict on a post that exists (names it, links it or quotes it): liked, disliked, wrong tone, pull it
feedback.acts: the Writer reads it in the digest; the same feedback twice becomes a Style rule (C6); "pull it" is the console's pull, not feedback
feedback.reply: Feedback on {id}: "{line}" ({link}), logged in the Feedback log. The Writer reads it in the digest; a repeat becomes a Style rule. Undo: revert {commit}.
